proposal_source: Consumed V3 HARK trajectory in which six same-response numeric-index edits produced two invalid later deletions and six partial-program replays.
research_question: Does one snapshot-relative atomic program-edit batch preserve the Agent's repair intent while reducing invalid edits and redundant replay without reducing Official success?
only_change_from_v3: revise_program accepts one list of edits, interprets every index against the pre-edit program, validates before mutation, applies the complete list together, and replays the resulting program once.

deterministic_qualification.macos_arm: 954 passed, 12 skipped; focused V4 interface suite 69 passed
covered_semantics: invalid batch leaves current program unchanged
one complete batch triggers one replay
V4 runner and tool schema are registered

live_hark_rerun.reason: HARK generated the proposal and is consumed; rerunning it would confirm a known repair rather than estimate effect.

next_live_comparison.control: Minimal B: continuous Agent plus repeatedly callable whole-program clean replay
next_live_comparison.treatment: V4: continuous Agent plus annotated operation-linked mutable program and transactional edit replay
next_live_comparison.selection: Choose a fixed paired batch before V4 outcomes from the pre-existing baseline failure census, stratified by candidate-formation and target-replay failures.
next_live_comparison.v3_ablation: Compare V3 and V4 edit efficiency only on prospectively observed episodes where plan revision naturally activates.

claim_boundary: The implementation and deterministic tests establish operation semantics only. No live effectiveness, generalization, SOTA, or efficiency claim has been made.
